evidence: Ter. And. 3.3.2: aliquot mē adiērunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A small number, not stated (Lewis & Short). With a word of time in the accusative, “for several …”: aliquot diēs.

terms.grammar: adjective, plural; gen. complūrium; neuter also complūria (mostly before Cicero)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “more than one, not a few”, with no comparative force. As a noun, several people: complūribus narrāvit, she told several people.

terms.grammar: adjective, plural (the comparative of multī); gen. plūrium
terms.comment: Properly “more” (see more); without a comparison it is “a number of, several”.

phrases.english: she told it to several people

phrases.latin: fonticulus in hōc, in fonte crātēr; circā sipunculī plūrēs miscent jūcundissimum murmur
phrases.english: there is a little fountain here, a basin in the fountain, and round it several small jets mingle a most pleasant murmur
